unit.title: Numbers Beyond 10 and Making Sense of Amounts

contentBlocks.text: Last week you learned to write 0 through 10. Today we go further — writing the numbers from 11 all the way to 20!

Numbers 11-20 are written with two digits — a 1 in front, and then the second digit changes each time (11, 12, 13...). Notice that 11-19 all start with '1' the same way, and then 20 starts fresh with a '2'. Practice writing 11 through 20, saying each number name out loud as you write it.
You now know how to write every number from 0 to 20! Tomorrow we'll practice taking groups apart instead of putting them together.

objectives: Write the numerals 11 through 20 with recognizable, if imperfect, formation
Notice that 11-19 share a leading '1' digit
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review writing 0-10 from last week.
2. Introduce 11-20, pointing out the shared leading '1' from 11-19.
3. Model writing 11-20 slowly, narrating each digit.
4. Let the child trace and write each number, saying its name aloud.
5. Close by counting from 0 to 20 together while pointing at each written number.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just 11-15 today, saving 16-20 for extra practice on the review day
Ready for more: ask the child to write the numbers in a different order, or count backward from 20
The two-digit structure is a genuinely new concept — take time to make sure the child sees both digits, not just memorizes shapes
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and writing-practice activity — there is no right/wrong answer beyond recognizable number formation.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core standard K.CC.3: writing numbers 0-20, extending last week's 0-10 practice to complete the full range this course's first unit introduced.

generationData.instructions: Trace each number, say it out loud, then write it once more on your own.
